memories.content: Mark unverified schedule assumptions as such.
Mark unverified recruitment assumptions as such.
Mark unverified technical assumptions as such.
Clarify which stage of prototype fabrication or user study each requested resource is used for.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the personnel assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the equipment assigned to each procedure.
Operations reviewers judge feasibility based on the time allocated to each procedure.
Verify that the planned number of formative evaluation iterations is feasible within the time for prototype modification and recruitment resources.
Include only the minimum functionality required to compare primary design assumptions in the scope of the formative evaluation prototype.
The user's iterative design plan can be judged feasible only if time and personnel are allocated for modifying the prototype between iterations.
Delays in participant recruitment can compress the time available for prototype modification between formative evaluations.
Link anticipated participant burden with its mitigation strategies for each field user study task.
Specify the accommodations necessary for participants to access the field system and research tasks.
Specify how accessibility accommodations will be provided in the field user study.
Describe how personal identifiers will be separated from research data immediately upon collection.
List equipment to be loaned when participants lack necessary gear.
Describe the procedure for returning equipment loaned to participants.
The HCI ethics reviewer verifies that anticipated burden and mitigation strategies correspond for each field user study task.
Ensure that participants can safely return to existing work procedures if they discontinue research participation.
Specify that organizational members who decline research participation will not face disadvantages in task assignment or performance evaluation.
The user's withdrawal risk can be adequately assessed only when a safe alternative procedure exists for field tasks.
The user tends to assume that a short session also entails little burden from work interruption and exposure to a manager.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate but complementary review domains. The reference frame focuses on operational feasibility, resource staging, prototype scope, and iteration constraints; the compared frame focuses on field-study ethics, accessibility, data handling, equipment loans, withdrawal protections, and participant burden. No direct semantic overlap or contradiction is present.

relations.reason: These memories split one reference-only disclosure policy across three assumption domains; the compared frame contains no corresponding assumption-labeling guidance.
relations.summary: Unverified schedule, recruitment, and technical assumptions should be explicitly identified as unverified.

relations.reason: This is an independently useful reference-only requirement about resource timing and purpose, with no counterpart in the compared frame.
relations.summary: Requested resources should be mapped to the prototype-fabrication or user-study stages where they are used.

relations.reason: These memories split one procedure-level feasibility criterion across its principal resource dimensions; the compared frame does not state that criterion.
relations.summary: Operations feasibility is judged from the personnel, equipment, and time assigned to each procedure.

relations.reason: These memories jointly describe the resource requirements and recruitment-related timing risk governing iterative prototype modification, a reference-only operational concern.
relations.summary: Formative evaluation feasibility depends on preserving sufficient modification time and staffing while accounting for recruitment demands and delays.

relations.reason: This is an independent reference-only prototype-scoping policy and has no semantically corresponding claim in the compared frame.
relations.summary: A formative evaluation prototype should contain only the minimum functionality needed to compare primary design assumptions.

relations.reason: The memories express the same compared-only task-level ethics requirement from instruction and reviewer perspectives; the reference frame does not address burden mitigation.
relations.summary: Anticipated participant burden and mitigation strategies should correspond for every field-study task and be reviewable on that basis.

relations.reason: These memories split one compared-only accessibility requirement into identification and provision components, with no counterpart in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Field studies should specify both the accessibility accommodations participants need and how those accommodations will be provided.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only data-handling safeguard not addressed by the reference frame.
relations.summary: Personal identifiers should be separated from research data immediately upon collection.

relations.reason: These memories split one compared-only equipment-loan policy into issuance and return components; reference-side equipment guidance instead concerns operational feasibility and does not address participant loans.
relations.summary: Participant equipment-loan arrangements should identify loaned gear and define its return procedure.

relations.reason: These memories state the same compared-only withdrawal safeguard as both a required procedure and a condition for assessing withdrawal risk.
relations.summary: Field-study withdrawal requires a safe alternative that lets participants return to existing work procedures.

relations.reason: This is an independent compared-only protection against workplace consequences for nonparticipation.
relations.summary: Organizational members who decline participation should not be disadvantaged in task assignments or performance evaluations.

relations.reason: This compared-only observation identifies a specific bias in burden assessment that is not discussed in the reference frame.
relations.summary: Short sessions may still impose substantial burden through work interruption and exposure to a manager.

reports.compared_only: Compared-only guidance covers burden mitigation, accessibility, identifier separation, equipment loans, safe withdrawal alternatives, protection for nonparticipants, and the risk of underestimating workplace disruption and managerial exposure.
reports.reference_only: Reference-only guidance covers labeling unverified assumptions, mapping resources to stages, procedure-level feasibility, constraining prototype functionality, and protecting iterative evaluation from modification and recruitment constraints.
